decisions.reason: As a close-to-core airport operations software with visible standalone positioning, it is a low-cost strategic option that fits the firm's push toward integrated, data-driven operations and should be kept while market feedback develops.
This connectivity module builds directly on the firm's installed base and integration capabilities, so the option value of keeping it on offer is high relative to the likely low cost of continuation.

Although billing software is somewhat less central than airside control products, it still extends the digital platform and should be kept for another year because uncertainty about customer uptake is still resolving.
Equipment monitoring software strongly matches the firm's engineering, maintenance, and lifecycle-service strengths, making it sensible to keep as part of the broader apron software stack.
This resource management module is close to the firm's established apron operations offer and supports the end-to-end automation strategy, so keeping the option open is the better choice.

The safety alert service is strategically attractive and aligned with the firm's tower and safety positioning, and despite potentially slower validation and sales cycles it is still worth retaining for further learning.
